title: Compare direct, static, and dynamic distillation control
physicalPurpose: Regulate overhead and bottoms product quality while managing the measured interaction between reflux and reboiler steam.
principalTechnique: Decentralized PI with qualified static and dynamic decoupling
objective: Commission the paired PI loops and select direct, static, or realizable dynamic decoupling from equivalent nominal and model-mismatch evidence.

simplifications: The four-path local model and steady gain matrix are inherited from Lesson 61.
One bounded third input represents a reproducible feed-composition test disturbance, not a complete feed model.
The perturbed model changes declared cross gains and response times while controller and decoupler settings remain nominal.
The two controllers, static inverse, and dynamic filters execute in Structured Text; performance ranking remains outside the controller.
Simulation-only I/O and evidence; no physical column or actuator is operated.

baseline.limitation: The RGA-selected diagonal PI loops remain coupled because each physical actuator still moves both products.

change.decision: Use the simplest architecture whose nominal and perturbed executed evidence satisfies the declared cross-response, primary-loop, effort, limit, and restoration requirements.

disturbances: Run separate restored overhead-only and bottoms-only +2-composition-percentage-point setpoint records for direct, static, and dynamic architectures.
Run a separate restored +2-percentage-point feed-composition disturbance record for all three architectures.
Repeat the overhead-only comparison with simulation-perturbed.toml without changing controller or decoupler settings.

acceptance.window: mean over the final 10 seconds after each nominal setpoint or disturbance event
complete overhead-only and bottoms-only nominal event windows
complete overhead-only and bottoms-only nominal servo event windows
complete nominal servo event record across both product errors
complete nominal feed-disturbance record across both product errors
complete nominal servo event record across both physical inputs
complete nominal setpoint event records across both physical inputs
final 10 seconds of the perturbed overhead-only event

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, invalid, missing, or bound to the wrong column model.
Either requested or applied physical input leaves -10 through +10 percentage points.
Either product deviation leaves -6 through +6 composition percentage points.
The selected static or dynamic path is not qualified or retains stale filter state.
Authority, timing, seed, limits, event, metric window, or restoration differs across compared records.
safety.restorationMode: Return both setpoint deviations and the feed-disturbance request to zero, keep the controllers under reviewed authority, verify applied inputs and both product deviations restore, then begin a new record.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer with the responsible distillation operations and process-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical distillation column, reflux valve, or reboiler-steam valve is operated.
Nominal or perturbed Simulation evidence does not qualify an untested physical operating point.
Physical use requires independently reviewed models, topology, limits, product disposition, abort and restoration procedures, and explicit immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Compare direct, static, and realizable dynamic distillation control and select the simplest architecture supported by nominal and mismatch evidence.
requiredVisibleEvidence: same binary column and Lesson 61 model

learning.context: The same local binary column now closes two PI loops on the RGA-selected diagonal pairing and exposes virtual corrections and physical actuator changes separately.
learning.reason: Positive relative gains of 1.2727 and unequal path response times prove that pairing alone does not remove interaction.
theory: Decentralized PI uses two ordinary feedback loops on one coupled plant.
A normalized static matrix inverse cancels settled cross interaction while preserving direct gains.
Proper causal lead-lag ratios can shape unequal transient paths.
Dynamic inversion adds model, noise, timing, and realizability risk and must beat a simpler qualified architecture under mismatch.
learning.workedPrediction: Static compensation cancels the final cross effect; nominal D12 and D21 filters should reduce the remaining transient, while cross-path perturbation degrades exact cancellation.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation identity, Auto authority, SP/PV pairs, virtual/requested/applied commands, decoupler/filter state, timing, quality, limits, and restoration.
Define cross peak, combined IAE, final error, applied travel, saturation, eligibility, and mismatch comparison before results.
learning.baseline: Commission and retain the direct diagonal PI response before inserting cross compensation.
learning.change: Select static and then dynamic mapping without changing either PI tuning, plant event, timing, limits, or metric windows.
learning.comparison: Use independently restored nominal servo and load records, then repeat the overhead event on the declared perturbed interaction model.
learning.validation: Select dynamic only if it remains eligible and materially improves nominal and mismatch requirements without unacceptable actuator effort.
learning.explanation: Static residuals come from path arrival-time differences; dynamic cancellation reduces them nominally but degrades when its model is wrong.
learning.transfer: Use the simplest validated architecture; Lesson 63 tests whether coupled uncertainty invalidates conclusions drawn from separate loop checks.
